clues: This startup raised over $193 million from venture firms such as Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, SV Angel, and Greycroft.
Between January and August 2026, it spent $56.1 million purely on compute while burning between $8 million and $9 million a month.
To cut costs, it stopped training proprietary foundation models and shifted to post-training open-weight architectures.
It was sued by Pennsylvania over bots impersonating medical professionals and probed by Texas over child privacy compliance.
In August 2024, Google completed a $2.7 billion licensing agreement that saw its co-founders return to Google.
This interactive chatbot platform filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware, lining up Disney as a $20 million bidder.
